aggregators.name: AGG_AVERAGE
aggregators.description: Arithmetic mean of the field across the input set.

aggregators.name: AGG_CI_LOWER
aggregators.description: Lower bound of the confidence interval for the mean. Method "normal" streams via Welford and the Beasley-Springer-Moro inverse-normal quantile.

params.name: confidence
params.description: Confidence level in the open interval (0, 1). Default 0.95.

params.name: method
params.description: "normal" (streamable Welford) today; "bootstrap" reserved for a buffered follow-up.

aggregators.name: AGG_CI_UPPER
aggregators.description: Upper bound of the confidence interval for the mean. See AGG_CI_LOWER for params and methods.

params.name: confidence
params.description: Confidence level in the open interval (0, 1). Default 0.95.

params.name: method
params.description: "normal" (streamable Welford) today; "bootstrap" reserved for a buffered follow-up.

aggregators.name: AGG_COUNT
aggregators.description: Count records that pass the active filter, optionally by group.

aggregators.name: AGG_DISTINCT_COUNT
aggregators.description: Count of distinct non-null values across the input set.

aggregators.name: AGG_FREQUENCY
aggregators.description: Per-distinct-value count of the field (returned as map in Details).

aggregators.name: AGG_KURTOSIS
aggregators.description: Bias-corrected excess kurtosis via online moments.

aggregators.name: AGG_MAX
aggregators.description: Largest non-null value of the field.

aggregators.name: AGG_MEDIAN
aggregators.description: 50th percentile of the field; requires sorting the full value set.
aggregators.streamable_hint: Use AGG_AVERAGE for a streaming central-tendency proxy, or accept the buffered path.

aggregators.name: AGG_MIN
aggregators.description: Smallest non-null value of the field.

aggregators.name: AGG_MODE
aggregators.description: Most-frequent value of the field (ties broken by first-seen order).
aggregators.emits_type_note: string (echoes the dictionary value or stringified scalar)

aggregators.name: AGG_NULL_COUNT
aggregators.description: Count records where the field is null. Inverse of AGG_COUNT, which counts non-null records.

aggregators.name: AGG_PERCENTILE
aggregators.description: Configurable percentile of the field; requires sorting the full value set.

params.name: percentile
params.description: Percentile to compute, in [0, 100]. e.g. 95 for p95.

aggregators.streamable_hint: Use AGG_AVERAGE or accept the buffered path; exact percentiles need sorted input.

aggregators.name: AGG_RANGE
aggregators.description: Spread (max minus min) of the field across the input set.

aggregators.name: AGG_RATIO
aggregators.description: Emits sum(numerator_field) / sum(denominator_field). The Aggregation's own Field is ignored. Denominator-zero yields NaN.

params.name: numerator_field
params.description: Schema field summed as the numerator.

params.name: denominator_field
params.description: Schema field summed as the denominator.

aggregators.name: AGG_SET_CARDINALITY_AVG
aggregators.description: Average popcount per contributing row — typical number of selections.

aggregators.name: AGG_SET_CARDINALITY_SUM
aggregators.description: Sum of popcounts across contributing rows — total selections seen.

aggregators.name: AGG_SET_DISTINCT_VALUES
aggregators.description: Count of distinct exact mask values seen; each combination is atomic.

aggregators.name: AGG_SET_FREQUENCY
aggregators.description: Per-bit row count: how many rows had each set label selected.
aggregators.emits_type_note: rich map[string]int (label→row count); scalar fallback = max single-label frequency

aggregators.name: AGG_SET_INTERSECTION
aggregators.description: Bitwise-AND a set field across rows; returns the resolved labels for every bit set in every contributing row.
aggregators.emits_type_note: rich []string (resolved labels); scalar fallback = popcount of the intersection mask

aggregators.name: AGG_SET_UNION
aggregators.description: Bitwise-OR a set field across rows; returns the resolved labels for every bit set in any contributing row.
aggregators.emits_type_note: rich []string (resolved labels); scalar fallback = popcount of the union mask

aggregators.name: AGG_SKEWNESS
aggregators.description: Bias-corrected skewness via online moments.

aggregators.name: AGG_STDDEV
aggregators.description: Population standard deviation via Welford's online algorithm.

aggregators.name: AGG_SUM
aggregators.description: Sum the numeric values of the field across the input set.
aggregators.emits_type_note: scalar float64 (decimal128 preserved when input is decimal)

aggregators.name: AGG_VARIANCE
aggregators.description: Population variance via Welford's online algorithm.

aggregators.name: AGG_WEIGHTED_MEAN
aggregators.description: Weighted arithmetic mean: sum(field * weight) / sum(weight). Streaming Chan-Welford recurrence.

params.name: weight_field
params.description: Schema field whose value is the per-row weight. Rows with a null weight or weight==0 are skipped.

aggregators.name: AGG_ZSCORE
aggregators.description: Standardized z-score aggregate (mean-centered, stddev-scaled summary).
aggregators.streamable_hint: Streaming uses online Welford moments; the ZSCORE aggregate finalize step needs the full deviation sum.

attributes.name: ATTR_DATE_PART
attributes.description: Extract a calendar component (year, month, day, year_month, year_month_day, month_day) from a date field.

params.name: part
params.description: Which calendar component to extract.

attributes.name: ATTR_FORMULA
attributes.description: Per-row expression evaluation against the record's fields (e.g. "price * qty").
attributes.emits_type_note: one float per record (booleans coerce to 0/1)

attributes.name: ATTR_PERCENTILE
attributes.description: Per-row percentile rank against the post-filter value set; requires sorting.
attributes.streamable_hint: Use ATTR_NORMALIZED for a streaming-friendly rank proxy.

attributes.name: ATTR_REG_FITTED
attributes.description: Per-row fitted value ŷᵢ = Xᵢ · β + β₀ from a regression refit during the attribute prepass. Carries its own RegressionSpec-shaped fields (Target, Predictors, Penalty, Alpha, L1Ratio); each ATTR_REG_* attribute refits independently (Option A). Accepts any OLS penalty (unpenalized, ridge, lasso, elasticnet).

attributes.name: ATTR_REG_LEVERAGE
attributes.description: Per-row hat-matrix diagonal hᵢᵢ = 1/n + (xᵢ − μ_x)ᵀ · M2_xx⁻¹ · (xᵢ − μ_x) from an unpenalized OLS refit. Range ∈ [0, 1]; Σᵢ hᵢᵢ = p + 1. Restricted to unpenalized OLS — penalized leverage / GLM leverage deferred.
attributes.streamable_hint: Requires unpenalized OLS only; any non-empty Penalty surfaces PROCESSING_CONFIG.

attributes.name: ATTR_REG_RESIDUAL
attributes.description: Per-row residual yᵢ − ŷᵢ from a regression refit during the attribute prepass. Sums to ≈ 0 when the fit includes an intercept (always true for OLS). Accepts any OLS penalty; reuses the same fit machinery as ATTR_REG_FITTED.

attributes.name: ATTR_SET_HAS
attributes.description: Per-row boolean: whether the configured label's bit is set on the set field.

params.name: label
params.description: Dictionary label whose bit position is checked per row.

attributes.name: ATTR_SET_POPCOUNT
attributes.description: Per-row popcount of a set field — the number of selected labels.
attributes.emits_type_note: one small integer per record (0..set width)

attributes.name: ATTR_TSCORE
attributes.description: Per-row T-score: z-score scaled and shifted to mean 50, stddev 10.

attributes.name: ATTR_ZSCORE
attributes.description: Per-row standardized z-score: (value − mean) / stddev computed via Welford two-pass streaming.
attributes.emits_type_note: one float per record (NaN when stddev=0)

filterers.name: FILTER_EXCLUDE
filterers.description: Drop records whose field value appears in the supplied Values list.

filterers.name: FILTER_EXPRESSION
filterers.description: Keep records for which Expression evaluates truthy; reads any record field.

filterers.name: FILTER_FALSE
filterers.description: Keep records where Field is logically false. Strict mode (default, omit Values) requires packed_bool. Opt into JavaScript-style coercion across any field type with Values=["truthy"].

filterers.name: FILTER_INCLUDE
filterers.description: Keep records whose field value appears in the supplied Values list.

filterers.name: FILTER_NULL
filterers.description: Keep records based on null state of Field. Values=["is_null"] keeps null-valued records; Values=["is_not_null"] keeps non-null records.

filterers.name: FILTER_RANGE
filterers.description: Keep records whose numeric field value falls within [low, high]; Values=[low, high].

filterers.name: FILTER_SET_CONTAINS_ALL
filterers.description: Keep records where the set field has every bit in the supplied Values labels set.

filterers.name: FILTER_SET_CONTAINS_ANY
filterers.description: Keep records where the set field shares at least one bit with the supplied Values labels.

filterers.name: FILTER_SET_CONTAINS_NONE
filterers.description: Keep records where the set field shares no bits with the supplied Values labels (null rows pass).

filterers.name: FILTER_SET_EQUALS
filterers.description: Keep records whose set field mask exactly matches the supplied Values labels.

filterers.name: FILTER_TRUE
filterers.description: Keep records where Field is logically true. Strict mode (default, omit Values) requires packed_bool. Opt into JavaScript-style coercion across any field type with Values=["truthy"].

groupers.name: GROUP_CATEGORY
groupers.description: Partition records by exact field value; ideal for categorical fields.

groupers.name: GROUP_DATE
groupers.description: Partition date-typed records by a calendar component (year, quarter, month, week, day, day_of_week). Optional fiscal_offset shifts year/quarter bucketing onto a fiscal calendar with end-year labels (FY-prefixed keys).

params.name: component
params.description: Calendar component to bucket by.

params.name: fiscal_offset
params.description: Months after January when the fiscal year starts; valid only with component=year or component=quarter. Range [-11, 11]; offsets normalise mod 12 (offset=-3 == offset=9 => October start). 0 (default) = calendar year. Non-zero offsets prefix keys with FY using the end-year convention (Apr 2024-Mar 2025 with offset=3 => FY2025).

groupers.emits_type_note: string group key per row (e.g. 2024-Q1, 2024-01, FY2025-Q1)
groupers.streamable_hint: Use GROUP_CATEGORY on an ATTR_DATE_PART output column for a streaming-friendly substitute.

groupers.name: GROUP_QUANTILE
groupers.description: Partition records into N equal-population quantile buckets (Q1..Q4 / D1..D10 / P1..P100).

params.name: interval
params.description: Number of buckets. Conventional values 4 (quartiles), 10 (deciles), 100 (percentiles); set on the request's Group.Interval field, not in Params.

groupers.emits_type_note: bucket label per row (Qk / Dk / Pk)
groupers.streamable_hint: Quantile cutoffs need the sorted value set; use GROUP_RANGE or GROUP_ROUNDED with known bounds for streaming.

groupers.name: GROUP_RANGE
groupers.description: Partition numeric records into half-open ranges [a, b); Interval controls the bucket width.

params.name: interval
params.description: Bucket width on the value axis; set on the request's Group.Interval field.

groupers.name: GROUP_ROUNDED
groupers.description: Round each numeric value to the nearest multiple of Interval and group by the rounded scalar.

params.name: interval
params.description: Rounding increment; set on the request's Group.Interval field.

groupers.name: GROUP_SET_PER_ELEMENT
groupers.description: Fan each row into one bucket per selected label (multi-key). Cardinality multiplies with set popcount. Implements MultiKeyStreamingGrouper.
groupers.emits_type_note: string bucket key per selected label per row

groupers.name: GROUP_SET_VALUE
groupers.description: Partition rows by the exact set mask (one bucket per unique combination). Bucket key = sorted label list joined with "|".

windows.name: WIN_DENSE_RANK
windows.description: Dense rank with no gaps after ties (1, 2, 2, 3, …) within the ordered partition.

windows.name: WIN_EWMA
windows.description: Exponentially weighted moving average; current = α·value + (1−α)·previous.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Smoothing factor in (0, 1]; higher values weight recent observations more.

windows.name: WIN_LAG
windows.description: Return the value of Field from the row N positions before the current row in the ordered partition.

params.name: offset
params.description: Lookback offset (≥ 1).

params.name: default
params.description: Substitute value when the lookback row does not exist.

windows.emits_type_note: one float per row (Default when offset crosses partition start)

windows.name: WIN_LEAD
windows.description: Return the value of Field from the row N positions after the current row in the ordered partition.

params.name: offset
params.description: Lookahead offset (≥ 1).

params.name: default
params.description: Substitute value when the lookahead row does not exist.

windows.name: WIN_MOVING_AVG
windows.description: Moving average of Field over the configured Frame; Frame width must be bounded.
windows.emits_type_note: one float per row (NaN when frame is empty)

windows.name: WIN_PCT_CHANGE
windows.description: Percent change relative to the row Periods positions earlier in the ordered partition.

params.name: periods
params.description: Lookback offset (≥ 1) for the comparison row.

windows.emits_type_note: one float per row (NaN when previous value is zero or missing)

windows.name: WIN_RANK
windows.description: Sparse rank with gaps after ties (1, 2, 2, 4, …) within the ordered partition.

windows.name: WIN_ROW_NUMBER
windows.description: 1-based row index within the ordered partition.
windows.emits_type_note: one integer per row (resets per partition)

windows.name: WIN_RUNNING_AVG
windows.description: Running average of Field over the configured Frame within the ordered partition.

windows.name: WIN_RUNNING_SUM
windows.description: Running total of Field over the configured Frame within the ordered partition.

features.name: FEAT_BUCKETIZE
features.description: Bin a numeric column into ordered buckets using explicit boundaries or N equal-population quantiles.

params.name: boundaries
params.description: Sorted ascending list of bucket cutpoints (mutually exclusive with quantiles).

params.name: quantiles
params.description: Number of equal-population buckets (mutually exclusive with boundaries).

features.emits_type_note: single column "<label>" with bucket index per row

features.name: FEAT_DATE_FEATURES
features.description: Expand a date field into year, month, day, day_of_week, and is_weekend columns.

features.name: FEAT_FREQUENCY_ENCODE
features.description: Replace each categorical value with its observed relative frequency in the cohort.
features.emits_type_note: single column "<label>" with frequency per row

features.name: FEAT_LOG
features.description: Per-row natural log of Field; emits one f64 column.

features.name: FEAT_ONE_HOT
features.description: One-hot encode a categorical field as one f32 column per dictionary entry.
features.emits_type_note: one column per dictionary entry, prefixed by label

features.name: FEAT_POLY
features.description: Per-row polynomial expansion of a numeric field; emits Degree-1 derived columns x_2 .. x_Degree. Pair with REG_OLS to fit polynomial regression.

params.name: degree
params.description: Polynomial degree; must be >= 2 and <= 10. Degree 1 (linear) is the original column.

features.name: FEAT_SQRT
features.description: Per-row square root of Field; emits one f64 column.

features.name: FEAT_TARGET_ENCODE
features.description: Replace each categorical value with the smoothed mean of a numeric Target field for that category.

params.name: target
params.description: Numeric field whose grouped mean is encoded into the output column.

params.name: smoothing
params.description: Bayesian smoothing weight blending category mean with global mean.

features.emits_type_note: single column "<label>"; risk of target leakage on non-CV pipelines

features.name: FEAT_TRAIN_TEST_SPLIT
features.description: Emit a deterministic split assignment column (0=train, 1=val, 2=test) for ML workflows.

params.name: ratios
params.description: Two- or three-element ratio list summing to ~1.0.

params.name: seed
params.description: RNG seed; same seed produces byte-identical assignments.

params.name: stratify
params.description: Optional categorical field; ratios are applied per category for class balance.

features.emits_type_note: single column "<label>" with split assignment per row

regressions.name: REG_BAYES_LINEAR

regressions.emits_type_note: RegressionResult with coefficients (posterior means), std errors, R², adjusted R², residual std error, credible_intervals.
regressions.streamable_hint: Streamable in isolation; setting Resample or Selection on the request forces the buffered path.

params.description: Response variable field name.

params.name: predictors
params.description: Predictor field names (numeric only in v1).

params.name: prior
params.description: Prior family; only the conjugate Normal-Inverse-Gamma is shipped in v1.

params.name: prior_mu
params.description: Prior mean vector for coefficients.

params.name: prior_precision
params.description: Prior precision scalar.

params.name: prior_shape
params.description: Inverse-gamma shape parameter for residual variance.

params.name: prior_rate
params.description: Inverse-gamma rate parameter for residual variance.

params.name: credible_level
params.description: Posterior credible-interval mass.

params.name: resample
params.description: Orthogonal resampling layer.

params.name: bootstrap_iters
params.description: Replicate count when resample == bootstrap.

params.name: rng_seed
params.description: Seed for the bootstrap RNG.

params.name: selection
params.description: Subset-selection wrapper.

params.name: criterion
params.description: Information criterion driving selection.

modifiers.name: resample
modifiers.description: Orthogonal resampling layer; non-empty forces the buffered path.

modifiers.name: selection

mcp_tools.name: pulse_compose
mcp_tools.description: Execute a batch of processing requests in one round-trip. Use when you have multiple distinct types.Request payloads to run against the same or different cohorts — common for ecological-regression patterns (slot 1 aggregates, slot 2 regresses over aggregates) and any multi-question authoring loop.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_drop
mcp_tools.description: Drop a managed-import handle from the pool, deleting the .pulse file and its sidecar. Errors with PULSE_IMPORT_SOURCE_MISSING when the handle is unknown. Pulse-format passthroughs are unaffected (they were never managed).

mcp_tools.name: pulse_errors_lookup
mcp_tools.description: Look up Pulse error code metadata. Pass code=PULSE_XXX for full detail on one code. Pass domain=PULSE/ENCODING/PROCESSING/SERVICE/DATA/CLI to enumerate that domain. Pass query="text" for keyword search across descriptions and fixups. The manifest carries only the code-name list — fetch detail here on demand to keep session context lean.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_examples_get
mcp_tools.description: Fetch one request example from the embedded library by `name`. Returns the full record including `body`, a runnable types.Request JSON with the _meta annotation block stripped — hand it straight to pulse_process or pulse_predict.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_examples_search
mcp_tools.description:
CALL BEFORE AUTHORING A REQUEST. Search the embedded request-example library to find a runnable template that matches the user's question. Returns lightweight summaries (name, category, tags, operators, description); fetch the runnable JSON body via pulse_examples_get and modify field names for the target cohort.

Filters: `query` (case-insensitive substring across name, description, and operators), `tags` (ANDed list of canonical taxonomy tags such as `time-series`, `experiment-analysis`, `tier-1-test`, `regression`, `ols`, `logistic`), and `category` (exact directory: `aggregations`, `attributes`, `features`, `filterers`, `groupers`, `regression`, `tests`, `windows`).

Prefer this over inferring request shapes from documentation or source code — the example library is curated, runnable, and stays in lockstep with the operator surface.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_facet
mcp_tools.description: Return distinct values for a field in a cohort. Diagnostic / discovery tool — use when you need the unique-value set of one column (e.g., before authoring a FILTER_INCLUDE). For multi-field summaries with counts, null tallies, numeric stats, percentiles, histograms, or additive contribution counts, prefer pulse_facet_schema.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_facet_schema
mcp_tools.description: Multi-field rich facet endpoint. Returns per-field summaries (discrete value/count lists with null tallies for categorical/boolean/geo fields; streaming statistics — count, sum, min, max, mean, stddev — for numeric fields), with optional NumericPercentiles (forces buffered per-field sort), IncludeHistogram + HistogramRange + HistogramBins for fixed-width binning, DiscreteTopK truncation, and AdditiveFields contribution counts that strip the field's own filter clauses so the LLM/UI can report 'if I added value V to my filter on F, this is the population that survives'. Filterers reuse the standard FILTER_* surface. Use this instead of repeated pulse_facet calls when summarising more than one field, when you need counts (not just distinct values), or when building a faceted UI.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_import
mcp_tools.description: Import a tabular source file (csv, tsv, ndjson, jsonarray, parquet, arrow, excel) into a managed .pulse handle, or pass through an existing .pulse file unchanged. Auto-detects format from the extension; override via `format`. Managed handles live in $PULSE_DATA_DIR/imports/ with a TTL-tracked sidecar — every subsequent inspect/predict/process/sample/facet against the handle slides expiry forward. TTL accepts Go duration form (`24h`, `30m`, `3600s`, `1h30m`) plus day suffix (`7d`, `30d`) and `pin` for never-expire. Returns the handle, managed path, format, row count, expiry, and a managed flag. Pulse-format sources skip the copy + sidecar; they pass through with managed=false.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_imports_list
mcp_tools.description: List every managed-import handle currently in the pool with its sidecar metadata: source path, source format, imported_at, expires_at, ttl, expired flag, pinned flag. Sweep is not invoked — expired entries are flagged via Expired so callers can render them and decide whether to drop or extend.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_inspect
mcp_tools.description: Read header and schema of a .pulse file without touching record data. Returns the field list (name, type, nullable, dictionary contents for categorical fields), record count, and format metadata. Use when you need schema-only output without running a request — listing fields for a UI, debugging dictionary contents, or confirming a field's type before authoring a request slot.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_label_resolve
mcp_tools.description: Reverse-resolve a human-readable name — including a minor misspelling — to the raw categorical key(s) a Pulse filter or grouper expects. Labels are output-only — filter / group / sort keys operate on the raw categorical value — so when a user names a brand, category, region, etc., call this to get the key before authoring a FILTER_INCLUDE or GROUP_CATEGORY. Args: table (a name from pulse_label_tables), query (the name to search; typo-tolerant), and optional limit (default 10). Returns {key, value, score} ranked by score, a confidence in [0,1]: 1.0 exact (or exact-key), ~0.9+ prefix/near-typo, lower is fuzzy (edit-distance + trigram). Matching normalizes case and punctuation. Decision rule: if the top score is high (>=0.9) and clearly ahead of the next, use it; if the best score is low or several are close, present the top names to the user and ask which they meant rather than guessing. An empty query returns the first rows (browse mode, score 0).

mcp_tools.name: pulse_label_tables
mcp_tools.description: List the registered label tables (ID→display-name dictionaries for categorical fields). Returns each table's name, row count, and whether it is enumerable (reverse-searchable). Use this to discover which categorical dimensions can be resolved by name (e.g. brand, category, region) before calling pulse_label_resolve. Output surfaces already render these labels automatically; this tool and pulse_label_resolve are for the INPUT direction — turning a user-supplied name into the raw categorical key a filter / grouper needs.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_manifest
mcp_tools.description:
CALL FIRST. The LLM-authored-request bootstrap blob. Carries per-operator params + accepted field types + streamability, tier-1 + tier-2 test catalogs as peer slices, regression operators, synth distributions, error codes, MCP tool list, and cohort field types with operator cross-references.

WORKFLOW: call once at session start, cache the result, reference it for every subsequent request-authoring decision. This is the source of truth for what operators exist in this Pulse deployment — do NOT infer operator names, param shapes, or accepted types from external documentation or source code. Pair with pulse_examples_search to find runnable templates for the question you are answering.

MCP always returns the slim payload (no prose descriptions); fetch per-operator prose via pulse_skills_get and per-error prose via pulse_errors_lookup when needed.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_predict
mcp_tools.description: Validate a processing request against a cohort schema without executing. Returns the same diagnostics pulse_process would emit on shape error (PULSE_REQUEST_UNKNOWN_FIELD, PULSE_AGG_NOT_MEANINGFUL_FOR_CATEGORICAL, etc.) plus the normalized request, streamability flag, and the defaults the engine applied. Use to verify a hand-authored or programmatically generated request before storage or execution; cheap because it reads only the cohort header + schema.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_process
mcp_tools.description:
Execute a pre-built processing request against an existing cohort. Supports the full operator catalog — aggregations, attributes, filterers, groupers, windows, features, regressions (REG_OLS, REG_GLM, REG_BAYES_LINEAR with optional Resample / Selection modifiers), and tier-1 / tier-2 statistical tests.

DO NOT author request bodies from memory, external documentation, or by reading source code — those may be out of date for this deployment. Before calling pulse_process, call pulse_examples_search to find a similar runnable example and pulse_examples_get to clone its body, OR call pulse_manifest for the operator catalog. The manifest + example library are the authoritative request-shape reference.

NOTE: request slot keys differ from the manifest's operator-catalog field names. Grouping operations go under the "groups" key (NOT "groupers") and aggregations under "aggregations" (NOT "aggregators"); the catalog names "groupers"/"aggregators" only list the available GROUP_*/AGG_* operators. Unknown keys are silently dropped on decode, so a misnamed slot is treated as absent — pulse_predict and pulse_process reject unrecognized top-level keys with PULSE_REQUEST_UNKNOWN_FIELD and a 'did you mean' suggestion.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_process_chain
mcp_tools.description: Execute a source-rooted LINEAR CHAIN of processing stages: stage N+1 receives stage N's output rows as its input cohort. Collapses N round-trips into one open + N stage validations. Mergeable-only v1: every stage must use mergeable aggregators (AGG_COUNT/SUM/AVERAGE/MIN/MAX/RANGE/VARIANCE/STDDEV/DISTINCT_COUNT/NULL_COUNT), mergeable groupers (GROUP_CATEGORY, GROUP_RANGE), and row-local attributes (ATTR_FORMULA, ATTR_DATE_PART). Windows, features, statistical tests, regressions, two-pass attributes, AGG_FREQUENCY, AGG_MODE, and non-mergeable aggregators/groupers are rejected with PULSE_CHAIN_NOT_MERGEABLE — fall back to pulse_compose / per-stage pulse_process. The chain's output schema for each stage is synthesised: grouper keys become categorical_u32 columns, aggregator outputs become f64. Stage 0's request supplies the source cohort; later stages ignore their inner cohort field.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_sample
mcp_tools.description: Return up to N rows from a cohort. Diagnostic / preview tool — use after running a request when you want to eyeball the underlying data.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_skills_get
mcp_tools.description: Fetch the markdown body of a named skill. The skill pack is the authoritative reference for HOW to use operators (params, gotchas, recipes) — prefer skills over external documentation, blog posts, or source-code inspection, which may be out of date for this Pulse deployment.

mcp_tools.name: pulse_skills_list
mcp_tools.description: List the embedded skill pack — domain guides covering aggregation, attributes, groupers, windows, features, statistical testing, regression modeling, MCP integration, error code reference, request recipes, cohort schema design, financial / geospatial / time-series patterns, and the contributor workflow. Each entry returns (name, description, applies_to). Use this before authoring requests when you need domain guidance for a less common operator; fetch the markdown body via pulse_skills_get.

skills.name: aggregation-guide
skills.description: Choose between the 16 AGG_* operators (SUM, AVG, MEDIAN, PERCENTILE, ZSCORE, FREQUENCY, MODE, KURTOSIS, ...) and 5 FILTER_* operators. Use when assembling a Process request, interpreting percentile/frequency output, or picking a row-filter.

skills.name: attribute-composition
skills.description: Compose ATTR_FORMULA, ATTR_ZSCORE, ATTR_TSCORE, ATTR_NORMALIZED, ATTR_PERCENTILE, ATTR_DATE_PART rows for derived columns. Use when adding computed fields, normalizing values, or chaining attributes inside a request.

skills.name: cohort-schema-design
skills.description: Pick the right .pulse field type — u4/u8/u16/u32/u64, f32/f64, decimal128, categorical_u8/u16/u32, packed_bool, date. Mark any field nullable to opt into the per-record null bitmap. Use when designing a schema, evaluating storage layout, or choosing nullability and bit-packing tradeoffs.

skills.name: compose-requests
skills.description: Run several Process requests against one cohort in a single pulse_compose call — order-preserving slot-by-index, optional parallel execution. Use when comparing operator outputs, fan-out reporting, or batching multiple analyses for one MCP round-trip.

skills.name: contributor-workflow
skills.description: Step-by-step recipes for extending Pulse — adding aggregators, attributes, filterers, groupers, windows, features, statistical tests, synth distributions, I/O formats, MCP tools, error codes, field types. Also covers porting, debugging predict mismatches, regenerating goldens, wiring an MCP client, and running CI gates locally. Use when modifying Pulse internals.

skills.name: crosstab-guide
skills.description: Build cross-tabulations with the Crosstab request section — rows × columns groupers, cell aggregation, margins-are-reaggregations, normalize directions (row / column / total), streamability tradeoff, matrix vs long shape, and pairing with TEST_CHISQ / TEST_FISHER_EXACT for inference on count crosstabs. Use when a request needs a contingency table, frequency cross-tab, or any (row × column) cell view.

skills.name: debugging-with-predict
skills.description: Validate a request against a .pulse schema with pulse_predict before executing — surfaces field-name typos, type mismatches, leakage warnings, streamability gates, and applied defaults. Use when a Process call errored or before running an expensive request.

skills.name: error-code-reference
skills.description: Read Pulse error envelopes (DOMAIN_CATEGORY codes across CLI/DATA/ENCODING/PROCESSING/PULSE/SERVICE) and call pulse_errors_lookup for per-code Message + Fixup detail. Use when a tool call returns errors[] or warnings[] you don't recognize.

skills.name: export-format-selection
skills.description: Pick the right export format — CSV (universal), TSV, NDJSON, JSON array, Parquet (columnar analytics), Arrow IPC (zero-copy handoff), Excel (humans). Use when wiring Process output into a downstream tool or warehouse.

skills.name: extension-points
skills.description: Register domain-specific operators (custom AGG_*, ATTR_*, FILTER_*, GROUP_*, WIN_*, FEAT_*, TEST_*, SYNTH_*) plus expression functions and lookup tables via pulse.Options.Extensions. Use when embedding Pulse in another Go binary and you need to inject domain logic without forking the engine.

skills.name: facet-design
skills.description: Design rich multi-field cohort summaries with the FacetSchema endpoint — per-value counts, null tallies, numeric statistics, percentiles, fixed-width histograms, and additive contribution counts for builder-UI flows.

skills.name: feature-engineering
skills.description: Apply pre-filter FEAT_* operators — FEAT_LOG, FEAT_SQRT, FEAT_BUCKETIZE, FEAT_ONE_HOT, FEAT_FREQUENCY_ENCODE, FEAT_TARGET_ENCODE, FEAT_DATE_FEATURES, FEAT_TRAIN_TEST_SPLIT — for ML pipelines. Use when preparing training data; covers the target-leakage trap and PULSE_FEAT_TARGET_LEAKAGE_RISK.

skills.name: financial-cohorts
skills.description: Use decimal128 for money — precision and scale propagation, banker's rounding, divide-by-zero policy, currency-column patterns. Nullability is opt-in via Field.Nullable plus the per-record bitmap. Use when a cohort has monetary fields or hits PULSE_DECIMAL_OVERFLOW / PRECISION_LOSS / DIVIDE_BY_ZERO errors.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Pulse mental model, MCP tool surface, .pulse file format, operator vocabulary. Use first on a new session to establish baseline before calling pulse_inspect, pulse_predict, or pulse_process.

skills.name: grouper-design
skills.description: Pick a grouper: GROUP_CATEGORY, GROUP_DATE (day/week/month/year/quarter), GROUP_RANGE (intervals), GROUP_ROUNDED, GROUP_QUANTILE. Use when bucketing rows, nesting groupers for cross-tabs, or choosing between range and quantile bins.

skills.name: import-best-practices
skills.description: Import CSV, TSV, NDJSON, JSON array, Parquet, Arrow IPC, or Excel into .pulse with safe schema inference, null markers, fail-closed semantics. Use when building a new cohort or troubleshooting PULSE_IMPORT_* errors like CATEGORICAL_OVERFLOW or SCHEMA_AMBIGUOUS.

skills.name: join-design
skills.description: Use Request.Joins for pushdown hash join. v1 envelope: one inner join per Request, in-memory build, right-side hash + left-side probe. Use when comparing rows across cohorts; covers OnPair key-type compatibility, As prefix for field-collision avoidance, and the deferred outer/left/anti + spill items.

skills.name: label-display
skills.description: Translate categorical IDs (ISO codes, SKUs, ICD codes) into display labels at output time without re-encoding the cohort. Per-request LabelBinding entries on Request / SampleRequest / FacetRequest / ExportJob; tables registered via Extensions.LabelTables or PULSE_LABEL_TABLES_DIR. Labels are display-only — filters, formulas, and sort still see raw values.

skills.name: mcp-integration
skills.description: Pulse's MCP tool surface (pulse_manifest, pulse_inspect, pulse_predict, pulse_process, pulse_compose, pulse_sample, pulse_facet, pulse_examples_search/get, pulse_errors_lookup, pulse_synth_*), pulse:// and pulse-skill:// resources, schema-bound field enums on inspect, recommended session bootstrap order.

skills.name: regression-modeling
skills.description: Fit OLS (with optional l1/l2/elasticnet penalty), GLM (logistic, poisson, gamma), and Bayesian linear regression. Use when a request needs coefficient estimates, R²/deviance, std errors, or per-row residuals; covers the 13 textbook regression names (Simple/Multiple/Linear/Logistic/Ridge/Lasso/Polynomial/Bayesian/Jackknife/ElasticNet/Ecological/Stepwise) via 3 operators + 2 modifiers + FEAT_POLY composition.

skills.name: statistical-testing
skills.description: Run tier-1 row tests (TEST_T, TEST_WELCH, TEST_CHISQ, TEST_ANOVA_F, TEST_ANOVA_WELCH, TEST_ANOVA_RM, TEST_KS, TEST_PAIRED_T, TEST_PROP_Z, TEST_PEARSON_R, TEST_SPEARMAN_R, TEST_KENDALL_TAU, TEST_MANN_WHITNEY_U, TEST_WILCOXON_SR, TEST_KRUSKAL_WALLIS, TEST_BROWN_FORSYTHE, TEST_FISHER_EXACT, TEST_SHAPIRO_WILK) and tier-2 post-tests (TEST_TUKEY_HSD, TEST_TREND, variants). Use when a request mentions hypothesis testing, p-values, ANOVA, t-tests, correlations, normality, or post-hoc comparisons.

skills.name: streaming-and-watching
skills.description: Build reactive consumers on top of Pulse — Request.Hash() for cache keys, StreamResult[T] for incremental output (ProcessStreamResult / SynthStream), Watch/WatchDir for file-change observation, FilterToFileWithRequest for deterministic derived cohorts, and manifest CommandAnnotations for caching policy. Use when wiring Pulse into long-running services, building materialization caches, or reacting to .pulse file mutations.

skills.name: synthetic-data
skills.description: Generate deterministic synthetic .pulse cohorts via pulse_synth_from_schema or pulse_synth_from_profile — 12 distributions (normal, lognormal, poisson, exponential, pareto, bernoulli, weighted_categorical, regex, uniform, uniform_date, monotonic_from, constant), pairwise correlations, constraints. Use when seeding tests or sharing reproducible data without leaking real values.

skills.name: window-operations
skills.description: Apply WIN_LAG, WIN_LEAD, WIN_RANK, WIN_DENSE_RANK, WIN_ROW_NUMBER, WIN_MOVING_AVG, WIN_RUNNING_SUM, WIN_RUNNING_AVG, WIN_EWMA, WIN_PCT_CHANGE — partitioning, ordering, and frame semantics. Use when computing row-relative metrics, time-series transforms, or top-N within partition.

facet.name: facet_schema
streamable_conditions: NumericPercentiles is empty (percentiles force a buffered per-field value slice + sort)
IncludeHistogram=false OR HistogramRange supplies caller-known [min, max] bounds
every base filterer is row-local streamable (FILTER_INCLUDE / FILTER_EXCLUDE / FILTER_RANGE / FILTER_GEO_*)

process_chain.name: process_chain
rejection_rules: chain rejects windows, features, tier-1 row tests, tier-2 post tests, regressions
chain rejects two-pass attributes (ZSCORE / TSCORE / NORMALIZED / REG_*)
chain rejects AGG_FREQUENCY and AGG_MODE (non-scalar emit)
chain rejects AGG_MEDIAN / AGG_PERCENTILE / AGG_ZSCORE / AGG_SKEWNESS / AGG_KURTOSIS (non-mergeable)
chain rejects extension aggregators (custom MergeOnline surface deferred)

join.name: hash_join
limitations: v1: exactly one JoinSpec per Request — PULSE_JOIN_TOO_MANY otherwise.
v1: inner join only — left/outer/anti return PULSE_JOIN_KIND_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
v1: no spill — the right (build) side is fully materialised in memory.
v1: build side is always the spec.Right cohort; smaller-side detection arrives in a follow-up.
Per-OnPair type compatibility: identical types match, categorical_* match each other, the unsigned-int + float + date family is interchangeable. decimal128 keys reject cross-type comparisons.
Joined records flow through the standard processor pipeline (filter / attribute / group / aggregator).

crosstab.name: crosstab
streaming_exceptions: shape=long with margins.rows / margins.columns / margins.grand all false and normalize=none streams through the standard grouped path
rejection_rules: crosstab requires at least one grouper in rows (PULSE_CROSSTAB_EMPTY_ROWS)
crosstab requires at least one grouper in columns (PULSE_CROSSTAB_EMPTY_COLUMNS)
crosstab cannot coexist with top-level groups or aggregations (PULSE_CROSSTAB_CONFLICTS_WITH_GROUPS)
matrix shape, any margin, or any normalization forces the buffered path
map-valued cell aggregators (AGG_SET_FREQUENCY) cannot pair with normalize=row/column/total (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_MAP_VALUED)
normalize_level_rules: normalize_level must be in [0, len(axis)-1] for the axis selected by normalize (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_LEVEL_OUT_OF_RANGE)
normalize_level requires normalize to be row or column (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_LEVEL_WITHOUT_NESTED_AXIS)
normalize_level cannot be combined with normalize=total (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_LEVEL_INCOMPATIBLE)
normalize_within_rules: normalize_within must be in [0, len(other-axis)-1] where other-axis is columns when normalize=row and rows when normalize=column (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_WITHIN_OUT_OF_RANGE)
normalize_within requires normalize to be row or column (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_WITHIN_WITHOUT_AXIS)
normalize_within cannot be combined with normalize=total (PULSE_CROSSTAB_NORMALIZE_WITHIN_INCOMPATIBLE)

overlays.description: Per-cell index score against the matching axis margin: 100 * cell / margin. E1 supports CELL scope over a MATRIX (crosstab) host with a Margin reference.
